newsitem.title: UK: Menswear retailer Blakes plans AIM float in August.
newsitem.headline: Menswear retailer Blakes plans AIM float in August.

text.p: Mens fashion retailer Blakes Clothing Plc said on Friday it planned to float on the London Stock Exchange's Alternative Investment Market (AIM) in August and pledged to expand its number of stores in the UK.
Essex-based Blakes said the flotation was part of a financial restructuring by its parent Formal Group Plc from which it will demerge. Formal stood to gain about four million stg from the float.
Blakes said it expected to be valued at 7.2 million stg at its issue price of 72-1/2p per share, with share dealing due to begin on August 6.
The company currently has 13 stores from West Yorkshire in the north of England down to Kent in the south, 11 of which are in covered shopping malls.
Blakes said it anticipated opening three or four stores a year in the medium term.
"The directors believe the company could be expanded to a total of 50 outlets throughout the UK over time," Blakes said.

The retailer sells mens casual wear and suits, with approximately 70 percent of turnover coming from brands such as French Connection and Ben Sherman. Own label garments account for about 30 percent of turnover.
Blakes made pre-tax profits of 1.15 million stg for the year ended January 31 1997 compared to 861,000 stg for the previous year.
Wise Speke Ltd have been appointed nominated adviser and nominated broker to the company.
